title: Proverbs, Chapter 14 (Leningrad Codex)
source: Leningrad Codex folios (Internet Archive, WSRP photographs) + tanach.us LC folio index + UXLC Hebrew + KJV
description: Proverbs 14 on folios 414r, 414v of the Leningrad Codex (1008 AD), the oldest complete Hebrew Bible. Hebrew from the UXLC transcription of this manuscript; English KJV.
introduction:
Proverbs chapter 14 from the Leningrad Codex (Codex Leningradensis, National Library of Russia, Firkovich EBP. I B 19a), copied in Cairo by Samuel ben Jacob and dated 1008/1009 AD, the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible and the base text of the Biblia Hebraica editions. This chapter stands on folios 414r, 414v.

This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: the specific folio side(s) carrying each section's verses, from the full-colour West Semitic Research Project photographs of the codex as redistributed on Internet Archive (item Leningrad_Codex_Color_Images, marked Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0). Folio-to-verse ranges come from the tanach.us LC folio index, which was derived from the West Semitic Research Project's published index; each section links only to the page(s) whose recorded verse range contains its verses.
  2. Original text: the verbatim Hebrew of this manuscript in the Unicode/XML Leningrad Codex (UXLC 2.5 build 27.6, tanach.us), a transcription of Firkovich B 19a with vowels and cantillation, released without restriction on the biblical text.
  3. English translation: the King James Version (1611, public domain), retrieved verbatim from bolls.life (KJV text, Strong's numbers stripped).
translator_notes: Ketiv/Qere: where the scribe wrote one form (ketiv) but the Masoretes read another (qere), the consonantal ketiv is given first and the vocalised qere follows in square brackets. פ and ס mark the open and closed paragraph breaks visible as gaps in the manuscript columns.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>חַכְמ֣וֹת נָ֭שִׁים בָּנְתָ֣ה בֵיתָ֑הּ וְ֝אִוֶּ֗לֶת בְּיָדֶ֥יהָ תֶהֶרְסֶֽנּוּ׃ <sup>2</sup>הוֹלֵ֣ךְ בְּ֭יָשְׁרוֹ יְרֵ֣א יְהוָ֑ה וּנְל֖וֹז דְּרָכָ֣יו בּוֹזֵֽהוּ׃ <sup>3</sup>בְּֽפִי־אֱ֭וִיל חֹ֣טֶר גַּאֲוָ֑ה וְשִׂפְתֵ֥י חֲ֝כָמִ֗ים תִּשְׁמוּרֵֽם׃ <sup>4</sup>בְּאֵ֣ין אֲ֭לָפִים אֵב֣וּס בָּ֑ר וְרָב־תְּ֝בוּא֗וֹת בְּכֹ֣חַ שֽׁוֹר׃ <sup>5</sup>עֵ֣ד אֱ֭מוּנִים לֹ֣א יְכַזֵּ֑ב וְיָפִ֥יחַ כְּ֝זָבִ֗ים עֵ֣ד שָֽׁקֶר׃ <sup>6</sup>בִּקֶּשׁ־לֵ֣ץ חָכְמָ֣ה וָאָ֑יִן וְדַ֖עַת לְנָב֣וֹן נָקָֽל׃ <sup>7</sup>לֵ֣ךְ מִ֭נֶּגֶד לְאִ֣ישׁ כְּסִ֑יל וּבַל־יָ֝דַ֗עְתָּ שִׂפְתֵי־דָֽעַת׃ <sup>8</sup>חָכְמַ֣ת עָ֭רוּם הָבִ֣ין דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וְאִוֶּ֖לֶת כְּסִילִ֣ים מִרְמָֽה׃
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>Every wise woman buildeth her house: but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands. <sup>2</sup>He that walketh in his uprightness feareth the LORD: but he that is perverse in his ways despiseth him. <sup>3</sup>In the mouth of the foolish is a rod of pride: but the lips of the wise shall preserve them. <sup>4</sup>Where no oxen are, the crib is clean: but much increase is by the strength of the ox. <sup>5</sup>A faithful witness will not lie: but a false witness will utter lies. <sup>6</sup>A scorner seeketh wisdom, and findeth it not: but knowledge is easy unto him that understandeth. <sup>7</sup>Go from the presence of a foolish man, when thou perceivest not in him the lips of knowledge. <sup>8</sup>The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way: but the folly of fools is deceit.

translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>אֱ֭וִלִים יָלִ֣יץ אָשָׁ֑ם וּבֵ֖ין יְשָׁרִ֣ים רָצֽוֹן׃ <sup>10</sup>לֵ֗ב י֭וֹדֵעַ מָרַּ֣ת נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וּ֝בְשִׂמְחָת֗וֹ לֹא־יִתְעָ֥רַב זָֽר׃ <sup>11</sup>בֵּ֣ית רְ֭שָׁעִים יִשָּׁמֵ֑ד וְאֹ֖הֶל יְשָׁרִ֣ים יַפְרִֽיחַ׃ <sup>12</sup>יֵ֤שׁ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יָ֭שָׁר לִפְנֵי־אִ֑ישׁ וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ דַּרְכֵי־מָֽוֶת׃ <sup>13</sup>גַּם־בִּשְׂח֥וֹק יִכְאַב־לֵ֑ב וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּ שִׂמְחָ֣ה תוּגָֽה׃ <sup>14</sup>מִדְּרָכָ֣יו יִ֭שְׂבַּע ס֣וּג לֵ֑ב וּ֝מֵעָלָ֗יו אִ֣ישׁ טֽוֹב׃ <sup>15</sup>פֶּ֭תִי יַאֲמִ֣ין לְכָל־דָּבָ֑ר וְ֝עָר֗וּם יָבִ֥ין לַאֲשֻׁרֽוֹ׃ <sup>16</sup>חָכָ֣ם יָ֭רֵא וְסָ֣ר מֵרָ֑ע וּ֝כְסִ֗יל מִתְעַבֵּ֥ר וּבוֹטֵֽחַ׃
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>Fools make a mock at sin: but among the righteous there is favour. <sup>10</sup>The heart knoweth his own bitterness; and a stranger doth not intermeddle with his joy. <sup>11</sup>The house of the wicked shall be overthrown: but the tabernacle of the upright shall flourish. <sup>12</sup>There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death. <sup>13</sup>Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful; and the end of that mirth is heaviness. <sup>14</sup>The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways: and a good man shall be satisfied from himself. <sup>15</sup>The simple believeth every word: but the prudent man looketh well to his going. <sup>16</sup>A wise man feareth, and departeth from evil: but the fool rageth, and is confident.

translation.original_text: <sup>17</sup>קְֽצַר־אַ֭פַּיִם יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה אִוֶּ֑לֶת וְאִ֥ישׁ מְ֝זִמּ֗וֹת יִשָּׂנֵֽא׃ <sup>18</sup>נָחֲל֣וּ פְתָאיִ֣ם אִוֶּ֑לֶת וַֽ֝עֲרוּמִ֗ים יַכְתִּ֥רוּ דָֽעַת׃ <sup>19</sup>שַׁח֣וּ רָ֭עִים לִפְנֵ֣י טוֹבִ֑ים וּ֝רְשָׁעִ֗ים עַֽל־שַׁעֲרֵ֥י צַדִּֽיק׃ <sup>20</sup>גַּם־לְ֭רֵעֵהוּ יִשָּׂ֣נֵא רָ֑שׁ וְאֹהֲבֵ֖י עָשִׁ֣יר רַבִּֽים׃ <sup>21</sup>בָּז־לְרֵעֵ֥הוּ חוֹטֵ֑א וּמְחוֹנֵ֖ן עניים [עֲנָוִ֣ים] אַשְׁרָֽיו׃ <sup>22</sup>הֲ‍ֽלוֹא־יִ֭תְעוּ חֹ֣רְשֵׁי רָ֑ע וְחֶ֥סֶד וֶ֝אֱמֶ֗ת חֹ֣רְשֵׁי טֽוֹב׃ <sup>23</sup>בְּכָל־עֶ֭צֶב יִהְיֶ֣ה מוֹתָ֑ר וּדְבַר־שְׂ֝פָתַ֗יִם אַךְ־לְמַחְסֽוֹר׃ <sup>24</sup>עֲטֶ֣רֶת חֲכָמִ֣ים עָשְׁרָ֑ם אִוֶּ֖לֶת כְּסִילִ֣ים אִוֶּֽלֶת׃
translation.text: <sup>17</sup>He that is soon angry dealeth foolishly: and a man of wicked devices is hated. <sup>18</sup>The simple inherit folly: but the prudent are crowned with knowledge. <sup>19</sup>The evil bow before the good; and the wicked at the gates of the righteous. <sup>20</sup>The poor is hated even of his own neighbour: but the rich hath many friends. <sup>21</sup>He that despiseth his neighbour sinneth: but he that hath mercy on the poor, happy is he. <sup>22</sup>Do they not err that devise evil? but mercy and truth shall be to them that devise good. <sup>23</sup>In all labour there is profit: but the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury. <sup>24</sup>The crown of the wise is their riches: but the foolishness of fools is folly.

translation.original_text: <sup>25</sup>מַצִּ֣יל נְ֭פָשׁוֹת עֵ֣ד אֱמֶ֑ת וְיָפִ֖חַ כְּזָבִ֣ים מִרְמָֽה׃ <sup>26</sup>בְּיִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה מִבְטַח־עֹ֑ז וּ֝לְבָנָ֗יו יִהְיֶ֥ה מַחְסֶֽה׃ <sup>27</sup>יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה מְק֣וֹר חַיִּ֑ים לָ֝ס֗וּר מִמֹּ֥קְשֵׁי מָֽוֶת׃ <sup>28</sup>בְּרָב־עָ֥ם הַדְרַת־מֶ֑לֶךְ וּבְאֶ֥פֶס לְ֝אֹ֗ם מְחִתַּ֥ת רָזֽוֹן׃ <sup>29</sup>אֶ֣רֶךְ אַ֭פַּיִם רַב־תְּבוּנָ֑ה וּקְצַר־ר֝֗וּחַ מֵרִ֥ים אִוֶּֽלֶת׃ <sup>30</sup>חַיֵּ֣י בְ֭שָׂרִים לֵ֣ב מַרְפֵּ֑א וּרְקַ֖ב עֲצָמ֣וֹת קִנְאָֽה׃ <sup>31</sup>עֹ֣שֵֽׁק־דָּ֭ל חֵרֵ֣ף עֹשֵׂ֑הוּ וּ֝מְכַבְּד֗וֹ חֹנֵ֥ן אֶבְיֽוֹן׃ <sup>32</sup>בְּֽ֭רָעָתוֹ יִדָּחֶ֣ה רָשָׁ֑ע וְחֹסֶ֖ה בְמוֹת֣וֹ צַדּֽ͏ִיק׃
translation.text: <sup>25</sup>A true witness delivereth souls: but a deceitful witness speaketh lies. <sup>26</sup>In the fear of the LORD is strong confidence: and his children shall have a place of refuge. <sup>27</sup>The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death. <sup>28</sup>In the multitude of people is the king's honour: but in the want of people is the destruction of the prince. <sup>29</sup>He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding: but he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly. <sup>30</sup>A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones. <sup>31</sup>He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker: but he that honoureth him hath mercy on the poor. <sup>32</sup>The wicked is driven away in his wickedness: but the righteous hath hope in his death.

translation.original_text: <sup>33</sup>בְּלֵ֣ב נָ֭בוֹן תָּנ֣וּחַ חָכְמָ֑ה וּבְקֶ֥רֶב כְּ֝סִילִ֗ים תִּוָּדֵֽעַ׃ <sup>34</sup>צְדָקָ֥ה תְרֽוֹמֵֽם־גּ֑וֹי וְחֶ֖סֶד לְאֻמִּ֣ים חַטָּֽאת׃ <sup>35</sup>רְֽצוֹן־מֶ֭לֶךְ לְעֶ֣בֶד מַשְׂכִּ֑יל וְ֝עֶבְרָת֗וֹ תִּהְיֶ֥ה מֵבִֽישׁ׃
translation.text: <sup>33</sup>Wisdom resteth in the heart of him that hath understanding: but that which is in the midst of fools is made known. <sup>34</sup>Righteousness exalteth a nation: but sin is a reproach to any people. <sup>35</sup>The king's favour is toward a wise servant: but his wrath is against him that causeth shame.
